answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network maps every agent identity as a vertex in an interaction graph anchored to cryptographic stake burning. Agents must burn collateral scaled by O(n^2), imposing superlinear economic friction on clone swarms. Like anchoring a coastal reef against storms or grounding root structures under a juniper canopy, this mechanism forces an exponential attacker cost curve that renders identity replication mathematically ruinous.
